summary: Summarizes the answers sites gave to the host questionnaire introduced in RFC 106. The chart shows how different hosts handle terminals, especially line-at-a-time versus character-at-a-time input and control characters. It was meant as background for people implementing Telnet. Dated April 1, 1971, but it is not a joke.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 112 introduces a summary of answers to a questionnaire about network hosts. It points out differences in how sites handle terminals, especially line-at-a-time and character-at-a-time input.

subtitle: A summary of ARPANET host questionnaire responses about terminal support.

tldr.problem: People considering TELNET wanted information about how different network hosts handled user terminals and control characters.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 112 attaches a summary of responses to the host questionnaire referenced in RFC 106 and highlights differences in terminal support.
tldr.outcome: The note offers background information for TELNET implementers and asks readers to report errors in the interpretation of a site's answer.

today: RFC 112 is an early summary of questionnaire responses about host terminal support. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that updates or replaces it.

sections.title: A Summary of Host Responses
sections.content:
T. O'Sullivan of Raytheon Data Systems introduces a summary of responses to the host questionnaire referenced as RFC 106 and NIC Note 5776. The attached chart contains the questionnaire responses.

The author says questions about terminal support were of interest to members of the User/Service Site Protocol Committee as they considered TELNET.
sections.plainLanguage: The note presents answers to a questionnaire about network hosts. The answers were gathered for people considering TELNET.

sections.title: Different Ways to Handle Terminals
sections.content:
The note highlights differences between line-at-a-time and character-at-a-time terminal handling, including sites that support both. It says the differences matter especially for control characters.

The chart is an attachment to the note; the text describes its purpose rather than reproducing the chart's entries.
sections.plainLanguage: Some hosts handle input one line at a time, while others handle each character as it arrives. The summary calls attention to those differences.

sections.title: Corrections to the Summary
sections.content: The author says the information may be useful as background for TELNET implementers. He asks anyone who finds an error in the interpretation of a site's answer to advise him so the chart can be updated.
sections.plainLanguage: The chart is background material, and readers are asked to report any misinterpretation of a site's response.

references.text: User/Server Site Protocol: Network Host Questionnaire, RFC 106, NIC Note 5776.
